faction.name: The Concord
faction.blurb: A fleet that votes. The trimaran carrier Long Promise and her Outrider: a mass driver, gunship wings and crews that mend. Officers serve aboard, and the Council pays for what it approves of.
faction.openingJournal: The broadcast reached everyone at once. The Council voted nine to four: the Long Promise makes for the Ion Reef gate.
faction.bossHail:
"Long Promise. A ship that asks its crew's permission. I have read your charter; it took four minutes and I found eleven errors."

"The Ninth Sentence holds this gate in the Prime's name. You may put it to a vote. The result will be the same."
faction.bossHailEnraged: "And the convoy you opened was counted. Every one of them will be counted again."
faction.winAhead: The Ninth Sentence breaks up behind you and the gate stands open. No other fleet has passed it. The Council is told, and for once nobody calls for a recount.
faction.winBehind: The Ninth Sentence breaks up behind you, but the Ascendancy's main fleet went through the gate while Mor held you here. You are through the Ion Reef, and you are second.
faction.winThirdAhead: Something else came through first, though. The gate's sensors logged it as weather.
faction.outpaced: Mor did not need to win. He needed to hold the gate until the Prime's fleet had gone through it, and he has. The Council votes to recall the Long Promise. The vote is not close.
faction.lostAhead: The Long Promise's last message is a list of names. It takes six minutes to send. The Ascendancy reaches the gate unopposed.
faction.lostBehind: The Long Promise's last message is a list of names. It takes six minutes to send. Somewhere a new crew is already voting on who goes next.
faction.briefing:
Nine days ago every relay in the Concord carried the same thing at the same moment: four seconds of nothing. Not static. Nothing, shaped like a voice. The Survey Board put a bearing on it, past the Ion Reef, and then the Board adjourned without a motion for the first time anyone remembers.

The Council voted nine to four to send a ship. The Ascendancy's Prime has simply ordered it. Something else is on the way there too, and nobody has been able to hail it.

You have the chair on the Long Promise. The gate at the far side of the Reef is held by High Inquisitor Calix Mor. The crews voted for you. Try to deserve it.
faction.rivalPasses: The Ascendancy fleet has passed you in the Reef. The Council has asked, politely, whether the chair needs help.
faction.thirdPasses: Something overtook the fleet in the dark. Sensors logged it as weather. The night watch has asked not to stand it alone again, and nobody voted against.

laterSectors.name: Sector II - The Kessane Drift
laterSectors.bossHail:
"Long Promise. The Prime has heard of you. That is not a thing that has happened to a Concord ship before, and it will not happen to another."

"I am the Hand. Where I close, the matter is settled. You have come a long way to be an example."
laterSectors.bossHailEnraged: "You opened the convoy. Nine thousand unlogged persons. The Prime felt each one leave the ledger."
laterSectors.arrival:
Beyond the gate is the Kessane Drift: the world the Concord and the Ascendancy broke eleven years ago, and the hulls of both fleets still turning around it. The broadcast is louder here. Half the night watch has started humming it.

The Prime has sent an Archon to hold the far gate. The ships out here are better found and better led, and every crew in the fleet has someone in that wreckage.
laterSectors.winAhead: The Hand of the Prime is open and drifting, and the Kessane gate is yours. Beyond it there is nothing on any chart, and the broadcast is very close now. The Council votes to go on. Nobody asks for a count.
laterSectors.winBehind: The Hand of the Prime is open and drifting, but the Prime's fleet went through the gate while the Archon held you. You are through the Drift, and the thing you came to stop is ahead of you.
laterSectors.outpaced: The Archon did not need to win. The Hand only had to stay closed until the Prime's fleet was through. The Council recalls the Long Promise. For the first time, the vote is unanimous.
